The primary material of a candle is typically wax, which serves as the fuel source. Common types of wax include paraffin, beeswax, soy wax, and stearin. The wax is usually molded around a wick, which is a braided cord, often made of cotton or paper, that draws the liquid wax up through capillary action to the flame where it vaporizes and burns.
